title: Numbers and arithmetic
subtitle: For the same candies, you can ask for an average or for full bags and leftovers.
concept: For the same candies, you can ask for an average or for full bags and leftovers.
intuition: 17 candies packed 5 per bag fill 3 bags, with 2 left over.

body.title: Use familiar arithmetic
body.text: Python uses + for addition, - for subtraction, * for multiplication, and / for division. For example, 3 * 5 gives 15 and 17 / 5 gives 3.4. Do not quote numbers. print(3 * 5) calculates before displaying. Multiplication and division precede addition and subtraction; use parentheses to change the order, as in (2 + 3) * 4.

body.title: Find full bags and leftovers
body.text: For full bags only, 17 // 5 gives 3. The two slashes perform floor division. For these nonnegative quantities, this is the full-bag count. 17 % 5 gives the remainder 2; here % does not mean percent. Three bags use 15 candies, leaving 17 - 15 = 2.

body.title: Reconstruct the original total
body.text: Multiply full bags by capacity and add leftovers: 3 * 5 + 2 = 17. If 20 candies fit 5 per bag, the remainder is 0. Change the total, then the capacity, one at a time. Counts are nonnegative integers and bag capacity must be positive.

formalDefinition.text: For this nonnegative-integer packing model, // gives full bags and % gives leftovers: bags times capacity plus remainder equals total.
conditions: Counts are nonnegative integers; bag capacity is an integer greater than 0.
The divisor for /, //, and % must not be 0.

derivation.text: total refers to 17 candies; size refers to capacity 5.

commonMistakes.correction: Ordinary division gives 17 / 5 = 3.4. In this model, // gives 3 full bags.
For these integer operands, % gives the remainder: 17 % 5 is 2.

With only 3 candies and capacity 5, can you fill a bag?
practice.hint: Less than one bag gives a full-bag count of 0.

learningCheck.question: Which operation finds leftovers when packing 17 candies with capacity 5?
learningCheck.explanation: A remainder counts what is left after filling all possible complete bags.
feedback: / gives the average 3.4, not the leftovers.
// gives 3 full bags, not the remainder.

furtherReading.title: Further reading: negative numbers and decimals
furtherReading.text: This packing model uses only nonnegative integers. Negative floor division rounds downward: -3 // 2 is -2, so the packing intuition cannot be applied directly. Floating-point arithmetic can also have representation error: 0.1 + 0.2 need not equal 0.3 exactly. The project stores amounts as integer cents; Decimal is an option for later study of decimal arithmetic.
